newsitem.title: USA: Primary Colors author Joe Klein gets new job.
newsitem.headline: Primary Colors author Joe Klein gets new job.

text.p: Psssst. Don't tell anyone, but Anonymous got a new job on Thursday.

Joe Klein, the political columnist who was unmasked as "Anonymous," the author of the best-selling novel "Primary Colours," will leave Newsweek magazine and join the New Yorker in December to write that magazine's "Letter From Washington."
The New Yorker said on Thursday that Klein will replace Michael Kelly who is leaving to become editor of the New Republic.

After denying that he was the author of "Primary Colours," a novel about a Bill Clinton-like presidental candidate of insatiable appetites, Klein was forced last July to admit he wrote the book after the Washington Post published pages from the original manuscript with his handwritten notations.
He apologised for his deception and has been actively reporting the 1996 campaign for Newsweek, where he has worked as a columnist for the last four years.
Dorothy Wickenden, the New Yorker's executive editor, said, "Joe is smart, original and tough. He will thrive at the New Yorker."
